Subject: Marketplace listing — procurement kickoff and invoice questions

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the intro over the phone earlier. We're ready to get the CloudRidge listing live on Redwood's marketplace and want to confirm the minimal "preflight" bundle you need from our side so we can get an initial PO routed and invoices flowing. A couple of specific questions: 

- For AWS Marketplace (transactable offering), do you need the partner/channel ID + tax forms up front, or can we supply tax docs after the first invoice?
- For Azure and GCP, what invoice recipient details does Redwood expect? (We have separate billing teams on each cloud channel.)
- Any preferred PO language / SKU naming convention so procurement's automated systems will accept the PO?

We'll upload W-9 and bank details to the DocuSign link you mentioned once we confirm the exact fields. Attaching a quick internal checklist we usually send to marketplaces — happy to adapt.

Best,
Elena Ortiz
Head of Finance Ops
CloudRidge, Inc.

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena@cloudridge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Jul 2025 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing — procurement kickoff and invoice questions

Hi Elena — thanks, great to connect. Below is the minimal preflight evidence + invoice-lane guidance for Redwood marketplace ingestion. I've attached a compact checklist (marketplace-evidence-checklist.pdf) — please use it as a one-page drop-in for your Finance and Channel teams.

Minimal preflight bundle (needed before published listing is transactable):
- Completed W-9 (US sellers) or equivalent tax form (W-8BEN / EU VAT ID).
- Payee banking details (bank name, ACH routing / IBAN as appropriate).
- Primary billing contact (name + email + billing PO mailbox).
- SOC 2 Type 2 summary OR attestation link (summary acceptable for initial go-live).
- Data processing addendum (if you process customer data).

Invoice lane mapping notes (what to put on the PO so our billing automation accepts it):
- For AWS: reference the Listing ID (REDWD-AWS-xxxxx) in the PO line item description and include your AWS Account ID on the PO header. Redwood invoices the marketplace and credits you per the channel flow; we need the Listing ID to match our ingestion rules.
- For Azure: include the Offer SKU and Marketplace Publisher ID; put “Azure Marketplace / Redwood Inference” in the remit-to field and send PO to marketplace-billing@redwood.ai.
- For GCP: include the Channel Partner ID and the Offer Name exactly as shown in the GCP listing. If you're transacting via a reseller, cc reseller billing mailbox on the PO.

Standard payment terms: Net 30 from Redwood invoice date (we can discuss different terms for enterprise deals).

Attachments: marketplace-evidence-checklist.pdf (stub)

Next steps:
1) Upload W-9 and bank details to our DocuSign link (or attach here if more convenient).
2) Confirm which clouds you want listed at launch (AWS / Azure / GCP) and the responsible billing contact for each.
3) Ben from Finance will confirm the final invoice-lane mapping and PO language we should provide to your procurement team.

I'll loop Ben on this email for the finance mapping.

—
Jasmine Liu
Seller Ops Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>

Also confirm whether we can accept a PO that references a single consolidated Redwood remit-to for multi-cloud deals (it will simplify CloudRidge procurement).
- Vanessa: want to know if there are any known exceptions for vendor-supplied bank account formats (CSV vs PDF), and whether our payments team needs a notarized bank letter for non-US IBANs.

I attached the one-pager I sent externally. If we're good, I'll send CloudRidge the DocuSign powerform link to upload W-9 + bank details and give them a sample PO template for procurement.

On timing: CloudRidge would like to be transactable in the next 2–3 weeks; they're flexible but want clear steps so procurement can schedule the PO.

Thanks — Jasmine
